NVDA.rationale: NVDA presents a compelling fundamental case: Q1 FY26 revenue of $81.6B (+85.2% YoY), EPS of $2.39 (+214.5% YoY), gross margin expanding to 74.9%, operating margin to 65.6%, and quarterly OCF of $50.3B on a near-zero leverage balance sheet (D/E 4.3%). The franchise is structurally dominant with 87.4% data center AI chip revenue share and 90% discrete GPU share. Critically, the market has not kept pace — P/E has compressed ~49% from its May 2026 peak of 63x to 31.9x, the lowest in the 365-day window, while earnings inflected dramatically. The new ACIE segment growing 31% QoQ vs Hyperscale's 12% reveals a broadening customer base that reduces hyperscaler dependency. However, several factors cap the score below +0.5: (1) net income exceeding operating income by $4.78B is anomalous and may overstate normalized earnings; (2) earnings yield of 3.1% still trails the 10-year Treasury at 4.71% in a tightening rate environment; (3) material competitive threats from Amazon Trainium ($20B annual pace), Meta in-house chips, and AMD's Azure expansion are medium-term risks; (4) China revenue headwind is worsening with Chinese companies planning to allocate ~50% of AI budgets to domestic suppliers. The Q2 guidance of ~$91B and FY27 consensus of ~$385B provide near-term visibility, and TSMC's capex raise confirms sustained demand. The PIT leak (Safe Superintelligence partnership dated 2026-07-27) has been excluded from this assessment. Score of +0.45 reflects strong fundamentals and attractive relative valuation offset by earnings quality questions, rate headwinds, and structural competitive risks that prevent a full +0.5.
